metric_text.construct: Testing mix (pyramid) and fast unit tests
metric_text.description: Favor many small, fast unit tests; fewer integration/service tests; and minimal E2E/UI tests. Keep tests focused and the suite quick and reliable.
Continuously and safely improve design guided by code smells: identify issues and apply appropriate cataloged refactorings while keeping behavior unchanged and avoiding cosmetic churn.

metric_text.construct: Simplicity, explicitness, and avoidance of over‑engineering
metric_text.description: Favor simple, explicit solutions; hide unnecessary magic/metaprogramming; keep configuration minimal and explicit; avoid speculative abstractions.

metric_text.construct: Minimal, cohesive interfaces and information hiding
metric_text.description: Expose small, client‑focused interfaces that encapsulate implementation details; decouple abstraction from implementation and provide clear, stable contracts that are likely to remain stable.
Organize code into cohesive, discoverable packages/modules with clear boundaries and appropriate visibility to keep APIs evolvable and maintainable.
Align with project/community idioms and local conventions consistently; deviations are rare, well‑reasoned, and improve clarity or consistency.

metric_text.construct: Eliminate ambiguity; be clear, precise, and accurate
metric_text.description: Write so statements cannot reasonably be misread; strive for clarity, precision, and correctness.
Explicitly state the reader background you assume, especially when writing for a niche or specialized audience.
How well the work identifies and reaches its intended readership, stating background and difficulty while remaining accessible beyond specialists.
Expose plausible discovery paths and methods so readers gain reusable strategies, while recognizing that discoverability is a symptom, not a criterion, of explanation.
Ensure proofs (including computational components) are of manageable size, documented, and reproducible so others can inspect and verify them.

metric_text.construct: Introductions and abstracts: strategy and quality
metric_text.description: Openings that orient readers—clear abstracts, accessible introductions, early communication of key results, calibrated ordering of results vs context, and framing of problem/aims/contributions.
Value unifying frameworks and transferable methods; integrate results with broader themes and illuminate via alternative approaches or reformulations.
Ensure legible, restrained math layout and page design: clear alignment and display/inline choices, minimal stacked scripts, effective headings/whitespace to aid navigation and readability.
Paradigms/exemplars, disciplinary matrices, anomaly–crisis dynamics, and semantic shifts in scientific practice.
Build from clearly stated axioms/definitions and derive results deductively in an abstract, axiomatic style when appropriate.
Effective use of structure, patterns, analogy, experimentation, and planning/adaptation to discover and develop results.

metric_text.construct: Figures and data visualization: design, integrity, and self-sufficiency
metric_text.description: Truthful encodings and clear design of graphics plus publication-ready figure/table quality with informative, standalone captions.

metric_text.construct: Integrating symbols into grammatical, readable prose
metric_text.description: Write mathematics in complete sentences that integrate formulas with proper grammatical roles, connectives, and punctuation; avoid symbol-only chains and misuse of articles.
For existence or realizability claims, provide explicit constructions or algorithms (step-by-step) when feasible to maximize transparency and usability.
Results/methods extend cleanly to related problems/variants and yield reusable tools, lemmas, or first applications; show adaptability and generative value.

metric_text.construct: Support by the description / no undue generalization
metric_text.description: Claim terms and breadth must be supported by the description; claims cannot generalize beyond what is directly and unambiguously disclosed.
A claim is novel if not anticipated by a single enabling prior-art disclosure; the subject matter was not previously known, used, or publicly disclosed before the effective filing date.

metric_text.construct: Written description — functional and parameter claims need concrete support
metric_text.description: Broad functional claims and claims reciting specific parameters (e.g., dosages) require disclosure of concrete structures/species or specific methods showing the inventor’s possession as of filing. Mere functional description, method‑of‑making alone, or aspirational results without an established structure‑function correlation are insufficient (e.g., University of Rochester; Ariad).

Infringement requires every claim element to be present. Map each limitation to the accused product/process, draft to control reading‑on of target products, and provide sufficiently specific notice when asserting infringement.

metric_text.construct: Filing formalities and language in regional/international practice
metric_text.description: Comply with language-of-proceedings/claim rules, nationality/residence indications, and national form/content requirements for foundational application documents; include required treaty references where appropriate.

metric_text.construct: Design application fundamentals — scope, claim form, and drawings
metric_text.description: Industrial design protects ornamental appearance only; a single design claim is required; drawings must meet design‑specific standards for views and conventions.

metric_text.construct: Background and problem framing in the specification
metric_text.description: Appropriately characterize relevant prior art/background, articulate the technical problem and shortcomings of prior approaches, and explain the invention’s technical achievements/advantages.

For AI/data‑driven inventions, disclose model/algorithm details and training data characteristics/procedures sufficient for a POSITA to practice and reproduce the asserted technical effects across the claimed scope; avoid black‑box omissions.

metric_text.construct: Generic‑computer implementation is insufficient for eligibility
metric_text.description: Merely reciting conventional computer components or routine computerization (including mere speed/efficiency gains) does not confer §101 eligibility.

Use one term per concept, define novel/technical terms, keep claims self‑consistent and technically sensible, and draft to give clear public notice; avoid coined/ambiguous phrasing and clean up sentence structure and references.
Address statutory and obviousness‑type double patenting; apply terminal disclaimers appropriately and understand their content, ownership tie, and effects on term/enforceability.

metric_text.construct: Life‑sciences eligibility — natural products, diagnostics, and treatments
metric_text.description: For biotech claims, address product‑of‑nature and diagnostic/treatment limits; show markedly different characteristics or specific, concrete applications to satisfy §101.

metric_text.construct: Design drawings — complete, consistent views and conventions
metric_text.description: Provide a complete and consistent set of views disclosing the design; use crisp black line drawings, correct broken‑line practice, and surface shading to show 3D contours; comply with design‑specific drawing formalities and jurisdictional/Hague nuances.

metric_text.construct: Application parts and formalities — completeness and structure
metric_text.description: Ensure the application includes all required parts in proper form (request/identification, title, §112‑compliant specification, at least one claim, drawings where required, abstract, oath/declaration, fees), in correct order/language, to secure a filing date and enter examination.

metric_text.construct: Unity of invention / restriction and election practice
metric_text.description: Ensure claims are directed to a single general inventive concept; apply and respond to PCT unity and U.S. restriction/election (including election of species, linking/joinder, co‑pending/RCE interactions, and double‑patenting considerations).
Title is clear, specific, accurate, and reflective of article content; understandable to broader specialists and aligned with likely search queries.
Exercises are accurate, well‑explained, diagnostically informative, and appropriate to the target learners’ experience level.
Title and abstract clearly and accurately convey the study’s scope, contribution, and relevance to the venue or domain.

Balanced discussion of societal impacts; analysis of fairness/disparate impact and mitigation; expectations for interpretability/transparency; ethical deployment framing; responsible-ML practices; and public-interest benefits/ROI.

metric_text.construct: Alignment of claims, evidence strength, and tone
metric_text.description: Claims and conclusions are warranted by adequate and reliable evidence; tone matches evidence strength and levels of evidence are indicated where appropriate.
Strength and correctness of analytical/mathematical methods and baselines; mathematical accuracy; and tight calibration of claims to evidence with appropriate causal caution.
Accessibility of materials and inclusivity of language to serve diverse audiences and needs (including non‑experts and readers with disabilities).

metric_text.construct: Model cards and deployment documentation quality
metric_text.description: Documentation for deployment clearly states intended context, limitations, training data, metrics reflecting real‑world impacts, and is accessible to multiple stakeholder audiences (technical and non‑technical).

metric_text.construct: Artifact availability, licensing, and FAIR discoverability
metric_text.description: Research artifacts (data/software/tools) have clear licenses, are findable in appropriate repositories/registries, and are curated for long‑term, interoperable reuse (FAIR‑aligned).

metric_text.construct: Clarity and specificity of research aims/questions/hypotheses
metric_text.description: The research problem, specific objectives, and (where appropriate) precise, testable hypotheses or predictions are stated clearly and at an appropriate scope.

metric_text.construct: Causal inference and generalization claims rigor
metric_text.description: Sound handling of causal claims and extrapolation, careful calibration of claims to evidence, and accurate statements about external validity/transferability.

metric_text.construct: Artifact availability, documentation, licensing, and FAIR reusability
metric_text.description: Accessibility, licensing, discoverability, and rich documentation/metadata and stewardship that enable verification and long‑term, interoperable reuse with stated intended uses/limits.

metric_text.construct: Systematic/scoping review design and evidence appraisal
metric_text.description: Appropriate and transparent review design, search/selection/synthesis methods, and structured appraisal/organization of evidence strength.

metric_text.construct: Positioning within and comparison to prior work
metric_text.description: Clearly situates the contribution in current literature, contrasts with relevant prior approaches/baselines or results, explains differences/novelty, and gives proper attribution.

metric_text.construct: Clarity and specificity of research aims/objectives/hypotheses
metric_text.description: The research problem and objectives (and hypotheses/predictions where appropriate) are stated clearly, specifically, and at a justified scope/need.
